title: Practice Again sheet spec
description: The content of one Practice Again sheet. scripts/sheet-worker/render_sheet.py turns it into the DOCX and the PDF through worksheet_lib, so the house style lives in the library and never in the spec. Prose: scripts/sheet-worker/SHEET-SPEC.md.

header.description: Override the running header outright. Default: ["ADRIAN'S MATH TUITION", the subject].

title.description: PRACTICE AGAIN — Learn from <paper>, or … from your <A Math|E Math> papers on a batch.

papers.description: Batch sheets only: the student's own papers, as one grey centred line under the title.

student.description: Full name — rendered as the faded-blue "For <Full Name>" subtitle.

instructions.description: Override the three fixed instruction lines. Leave it out.

working_space.description: Blank writing lines per mark. A Practice Again sheet is read, not written on — leave it at 0.

parts.description: One paragraph's inline content: text pieces, equation objects, and Adrian's green rule tags. If it is maths, it is an equation object — a fraction typed with a slash is refused at save.

m.description: LaTeX. \frac, never \tfrac (\tfrac renders as a linear fraction). End a line with \quad\text{← note} for the grey 8 pt arrow annotation.

oneOf.description: Adrian's [rule in green bold square brackets]. Pieces are strings or {"m": latex} — the maths inside a tag is an equation object like everywhere else.

color.description: 00B050 the rule and its result (default), 0432FF the expression being matched, EE0000 the piece added or changed.

style.description: Reproduce an existing sheet's exact ink on a line whose styling has varied. Leave it out on a new sheet — the house default is right.

source.description: Where a figure's pixels come from: rendered from a figure_lib spec, or a file beside the spec (a bank question's own diagram, or a bespoke matplotlib render).

glue.description: Keep this paragraph with the one after it. The headings glue themselves; use this only to reproduce a sheet that glued more.

new_page.description: Open a page. Default: every skill after the first does, so a section is read whole.

then.description: The Title Case section heading, bold navy. It names the TOOL, not the task.
Batch sheets only: the grey line "Where it showed: 2025 Paper 1 Q2 and Q8(a)".
The ONE blue key-move line under the heading. The situation goes here, not in the heading.

label.description: null → the next number; "a" opens a lettered group, "b" reuses its number.

indent_cm.description: Line this paragraph up with the text of the numbered question above it (1.0), rather than with the number.

then.description: An unnumbered paragraph — an Example's stem, a continuation line under a practice question.
Opens the (a)(b)(c) list under an Example's unnumbered stem, flush with its left edge. Call it after the stem and its figure.
(a) / (b) / (c) — under an Example after parts_start, or under the practice item above it.
A numbered practice question, 1. 2. 3. — never (a) (b) (c). A question with parts uses part blocks under it and ONE answer at the end.
"Practice N" — restarts the numbering so every set counts 1, 2, 3 from the top.
A hint UNDER a practice question, grey: [Remember: …]. The brackets are added.
ONE orange right-aligned [Ans: …] at the END of the whole question, carrying every part. The brackets and the "Ans: " are added. Answers are equation objects too.
A diagram under the question that uses it. A QUESTION carries a diagram only when the bank question itself has one; a diagram you draw goes inside the solution box.

glue.description: Keep the "Solution:" label with the box below it.

keep_together.description: Default false — on a teaching sheet the box flows, or a block that does not fit jumps whole to the next page and leaves half a page blank.

label.description: (a) / (i) — or "" for a one-part solution, which becomes a single full-width cell.

then.description: The boxed worked solution: outer border only, the part label in its own narrow column, one row per part.
A data table the question comes with — a two-way frequency table, an ingredient list, a table to fill in. Full gridlines, unlike a solution box.
One empty body line. The library already spaces the boxes; use this only where a sheet needs air of its own.
A hard page break — before a new skill, when the sheet wants one.

step.description: One line inside a solution box.

then.description: A grey italic principle line. A box opens with 2–3 of them: the general rule, then the move, then it applied to this question.
A step that says what you are doing, in plain Singapore classroom English. The general rule inside it is a green tag.
A display equation. Multi-step working is ONE \begin{aligned} block with &= per line, so the = signs stack; three = signs on one line is not allowed.
A diagram inside the box, on the first part that uses it, showing only what that part has established.
A sanity check, rendered "✓ Check: …" in green so the student can see it is not part of the working. Only where a real check exists.

The one red Common Error line: a concrete wrong MOVE a student makes here and what belongs instead, in one sentence. Most boxes carry none; two per sheet is plenty. The "Common Error: " label is added.
